fields.sample_size: documentary analysis of the 2020 reform (Law 14,026/2020) and the pre-2020 sector: 5,570 municipalities (70% served by State-owned companies, 25% municipal public companies, 5% private operators); 72 subnational regulatory agencies by September 2020 (34 municipal, 13 regional, 25 State) covering 3,785 municipalities and 77% of the population
fields.effect_estimate: Before 2020 the sector was constrained by fragmented institutional arrangements and regulation (many municipal agencies with fewer than 10 staff; some State agencies regulate more than 300 municipalities), low public investment including by State companies, and barriers to private entry; over 100 million people lack sewage collection and treatment and over 35 million lack piped water. The 2020 reform (national reference standards by the ANA, regionalisation, mandatory tenders, universalisation targets for 2033) could change sector structure substantially but, the authors expect, more slowly than the reformers anticipated. Written by staff of the national agency (views are personal). Descriptive legal-institutional analysis; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: legal and institutional analysis of a national reform (documentary)
fields.section: Full text: State of the sector before 2020; regulation (agencies); the 2020 reform provisions; Conclusion
fields.exact_location: State of the sector before 2020; regulation (agencies); the 2020 reform provisions; Conclusion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a legal-institutional analysis of Brazil's 2020 water and sanitation reform by authors from the national agency, read in full text 2026-10-04. Fragmentation, low investment and entry barriers explain the gap; the reform's regionalisation, national reference standards and tendering are expected to help more slowly than anticipated. No empirical evaluation.
